defects.title: The objective coefficient of a reverse-only reaction keeps the sign of the irreversible model
defects.trigger: model = createModel({'R1';'R2';'R3';'R4';'R5'}, {'r1';'r2';'r3';'r4';'r5'}, {' -> A'; 'A <=> B'; 'B -> '; 'C -> A'; 'C -> '}, [], [0; -10; 0; -4; 0], [10; 10; 10; 0; 10]); model.c = [0; 0; 0; -1; 0]; irr = convertToIrreversible(model); rev = convertToReversible(irr); optimizeCbModel of model, irr and rev (glpk)
defects.observed: (R2025a, 2026-11-25) objective 4 for model and irr, 0 for rev: S column and bounds of R4_r are negated back (rev.lb(4) = -4, rev.ub(4) = 0, rev.S(:,4) = model.S(:,4)) but rev.c(4) = 1 keeps the sign convertToIrreversible gave it (model.c(4) = -1)
defects.expected: rev.c(4) = -1: the reversible model describes the same problem (objective coefficient flipped with the S column and bounds, as convertToIrreversible does: 'otherwise the target changes')

notes: Lead decision: severity. The help lists only rxns, lb, ub and S under 'Fields used', so a strict reading could call the unflipped c a limitation; I graded wrong-result because the output is documented as the reversible form of the input model and its FBA optimum changes (4 -> 0) on a documented input (a _r reaction with a nonzero objective). Rest of the round trip checked in the probe: R2 restored to [-10, 10], _b removed, ids untagged, match removed, reversibleModel true. No src caller of convertToReversible. A legacy round-trip check in testModelManipulationOri.m is commented out (no existing test). The reproduction builds the model with createModel, which runs addMultipleReactions (quarantined); the model it builds is the one stated, and convertToReversible itself does not reach addReaction/addMultipleReactions.
confirmed_by: lead, 2026-11-25: c of a reverse-only _r reaction not flipped with its column, optimum 4 -> 0 (writer reproduced); wrong-result confirmed; default reach

defects.title: Reactions that keep all their species get their reactant/product IDs and aliases sorted apart, so IDs and aliases no longer match
defects.observed: (R2025a, 2026-11-25) in 12 reactions without itp[c] the i-th secondary reactant/product ID no longer belongs to the i-th alias (32 pairs); e.g. GAPD reactants {s4410 nad[c], s5962 pi[c]} with aliases {sa31, sa30} in the input (molID(sa31) = s4410) and {sa30, sa31} in the output. Lines 155, 190, 235, 275 rebuild every list with setdiff, which sorts IDs and aliases independently; transformMap2XML writes rxnReactantID{r}{x} and rxnReactantAlias{r}{x} into the same reactantLink
defects.expected: reactions whose species are all kept unchanged; the i-th ID still belongs to the i-th alias (help: only entries of removed species/aliases are stripped)

notes: Tier 1 (ledger says 3): no solver. Reproduction check: for r = 1:numel(m3.rxnID), for each x, compare m3.molID{strcmp(m3.molAlias, m3.rxnReactantAlias{r}{x})} with m3.rxnReactantID{r}{x} (and the product lists) -> 32 mismatches. Other observations for the full test later: the same lines also turn empty '' lists of untouched reactions into [] (double) or a 1x0 cell; rebase = 0 (line 77) makes lines 141-147, 176-182, 217-227, 257-267 dead code; lines 165 and 205 are unreachable (an empty base list errors at lines 137/172 first); the warning branches need a reaction with several base reactants/products. No warning fired when removing any single species of the shipped map. No src caller.
confirmed_by: lead, 2026-11-25: setdiff sorts IDs and aliases separately, mismatching ID/alias pairs (writer reproduced); default reach
